Open Food Facts covers packaged food. USDA FoodData Central covers plain ingredients, and needs a free key of your own. This app will not ship one: a key inside an open source app is a shared quota in a public repository.
Nothing here yet. Add a food you eat often, or look one up online and keep it.
Everything is per 100 grams, which is how labels are written and how this app stores it.
A name and the calories per 100 grams are all that is needed.
Get a free key at %1$s and paste it here. It stays on this phone. Leave it empty to clear it.
Log a weight first. A goal needs a starting point to measure from.

The line has been flat for a couple of weeks. That is a plateau, not a failure, and it usually means intake has crept back up to maintenance.

Off unless you turn it on, and off again next time. The card shows how far you have come, not what the scale says.

No account · No ads · Stored on this device
Track the trend without an account, ads, or a subscription. Your readings stay on this phone.
This is only used to work out BMI, body fat and roughly how many calories you burn. Skip it and everything else still works.
One reading is enough to start. The trend line needs about a week before it means much, so weigh in when you can and ignore the daily jumps until then.
Set a target and WeightTrack works out a finish date from the rate you actually manage, then breaks the journey into milestones. You can change it or drop it at any time.
Photos stay on this phone and are never uploaded. Pick two to see them side by side with the weight change between them.
That looks like %1$s rather than you.
That is a long way from your last reading. Record it anyway?
A scale that broadcasts its weight needs no tap here. One that does not is connected to when you pick it.
A household shares a scale more often than it shares a phone. Each person keeps their own readings, goal, measurements and history.
Sync this profile with Health Connect
Health Connect keeps one set of weights for whoever owns the phone, so only one profile can use it.

Off by default. Turn it on and a Foods screen appears, with your own foods, recipes and lookups against Open Food Facts. Meals are passed to Health Connect if you allow it, and never read back from it.
Weights are stored in grams, so switching units never changes a single reading.
A shorter window follows the scale more closely.
Only used to work out BMI, body fat and how many calories you burn. It never leaves the phone.
A short note on how the week went, and nothing at all in a week with too few readings to say anything honest about.
WeightTrack has no account and no server. Cloud backup is switched off on purpose, so these files are how your history moves to a new phone.
Import a CSV from another app
Exports from Libra, Happy Scale, openScale, MyFitnessPal, Renpho, Withings and most others are read automatically. Columns are matched by name and the date format is worked out from the file.
If the app ever closes unexpectedly, the details are written to a file here so you can send them on. Nothing is uploaded on its own.
Free and open source under the MIT licence. No ads, no subscription, no account, and nothing about you is sent anywhere.
You will not be nudged on a day you have already weighed in.
Android is holding WeightTrack to approximate alarms, so the reminder may arrive a little late. Allowing exact alarms fixes that.
If reminders stop arriving, check that battery optimisation is turned off for WeightTrack. Samsung and Xiaomi phones are the usual culprits.
Health Connect is not available on this device, so scale apps cannot hand readings over automatically. Everything else works as normal.
Health Connect needs updating before WeightTrack can talk to it.
Pulls readings in from Withings, Renpho, Samsung Health, Fitbit and anything else that writes weight, and sends yours back out. Records are matched on both sides, so nothing is ever imported twice.
Readings older than a month, meals, drinks and steps are not shared yet. They each need their own permission.

No account and nothing of yours on anybody\'s server but your own. Each device writes one file and reads the others, so put that folder somewhere both phones can see: a Syncthing folder, or a directory on your own Nextcloud.
About once an hour when the phone is charging or idle. There is always the button.
On Nextcloud, make an app password rather than using your account one. It is kept on this phone and sent to that server and nowhere else.
The serving is what the big button and the home screen widget add.

This scale has forgotten the pairing, which happens after a factory reset or a battery change. Your phone still holds its half, so it connects and then goes quiet. Forget the scale in Android\'s Bluetooth settings and pair it again.

Pick a folder and WeightTrack writes a copy of everything into it once a week, keeping the last four. Cloud backup is switched off on purpose, so this is the only copy that exists unless you make one yourself.

A straight line is fitted to your smoothed trend over that many days, and the distance left is divided by it. Nothing else goes into it: not your height, not your age, and not what you say you eat. Change how fast you are going and the date moves with you.
You are already there, so there is nothing left to project.
There are not enough weigh-ins yet to fit a rate to. A week or two of readings and a date will appear.
Your trend is level, so there is no rate to divide the remaining distance by. A date here would be invented rather than worked out.
Your trend is moving away from the target, so at this rate it never arrives. That is worth knowing rather than being given a date anyway.
At this rate the answer is years away, which is a guess rather than a forecast, so no date is offered.
The folder is no longer reachable, so no copy has been taken. Choose it again to start them up.
Keep only the lowest reading each day
A second weigh-in after breakfast is the same morning plus a meal, not a second day. With this on, a day with several readings in Health Connect brings in the lowest one.
